errors.description: Candidate-4 does not match the on-file tech-pack illustration (which shows an open spread collar with pointed fold-over leaves). This divergence is INTENTIONAL: the owner rejected attempt 3 on 2026-08-10 with tags 'Wrong garment or wrong part' and 'Reference drawing itself is wrong', disqualifying the drawing as geometry authority. Candidate-4 was generated from the catalog label/description instead: 'A band-style stand collar finished with a faceted, six-sided geometric profile at the closure.' QC cannot certify blueprint fidelity because no valid blueprint exists for this option — the finding is recorded so the verdict routes to the owner rather than shipping unadjudicated.
errors.expected: A trustworthy tech-pack drawing of the Hexagon Stand Collar to grade against (the current drawing depicts a different collar family and is owner-disqualified).
errors.actual: An upright closed band/stand collar, fastened at center front with a six-sided hexagonal faceted closure, matching the catalog description and the owner's part-lock — but verifiable only against prose, not a drawing.
errors.correction: Owner adjudication required: either approve candidate-4's stand-collar interpretation, or supply a corrected tech-pack drawing / reference photo for the Hexagon Stand Collar. Do not regenerate until the drawing authority is fixed — regeneration cannot resolve a disqualified blueprint.

errors.description: The hexagonal profile is executed as an applied hexagonal closure tab carrying the button at center front. The catalog prose ('faceted, six-sided geometric profile at the closure') could alternatively be read as the band's own front ends being cut into facets. Both readings are plausible; only the owner can confirm which execution is intended.
errors.expected: Owner-confirmed execution of the six-sided closure detail.
errors.actual: Hexagonal stitched closure tab, centered on the placket, crisp straight facets, sharp corners, even edge-stitching.
errors.correction: If the owner prefers faceted band-ends over an applied tab, say so in the next correction round (ideally with a reference photo).
